pillar_reactions.evidence: Rep tied it directly to his stiffness and his treatment schedule — 'all you need is like 30 to 40 minutes, three to four times a week, tops... for you, that's especially important for that upcoming battles that you're gonna have to fight' — and closed with 'Does this sound like an approach that you've been looking for?' Prospect answered 'Yeah, 100%, yeah' with no questions and no elaboration.

Rep pre-empted it as already handled: 'you already have it dialed in because you're doing keto. And actually, it's very similar to what Trevor is coaching', then gave the three-variable frame and the once-a-week day off. Prospect: 'It's good, yeah. It sounds good.' Notably nobody raised that the prospect's ketogenic diet was adopted since surgery and is likely part of his cancer strategy, or that a weekly pizza cuts across it.

The only pillar he volunteered a positive reaction to and tied to his own situation: 'It would be huge, because then I have guidance. I mean, well, work as a coach, so I know how easy... Having someone next to you to guide you through them, their movements and what I'm doing right What I'm doing wrong, and have the training set up and everything, it makes it way easier.' The rep had set it up by leaning on his own profession — 'you're a coach, so you probably understand how coaching important is'.

anchors.raw: I'm paying everything privately. I'm paying, like, radiotherapy, chemotherapy, and those things cost a fortune. So all my savings are going through cancer sheets, and doctors, and blood exams, and MRIs, and supplements.
anchors.note: The competing spend is his own cancer treatment, self-funded because he is a non-resident in Australia. Every dollar to the programme is a dollar out of a treatment fund whose future size is unknown, which is why he would not name a figure.

anchors.raw: the amount of money that we're going to have to pay for the chemo, we are not really sure yet of the exams, how often we're going to have to do blood tests. So it's hard to commit for, like, big investments when you have something like I do.
anchors.note: Not a price objection but an unquantifiable-liability objection. No discount or instalment structure fixes it, because the blocker is that the denominator is unknown. The rep did not respond to this at all.

anchors.raw: I wasn't aware of the price at all. don't know, it was, like, thousands and thousands of dollars.
anchors.note: He arrived with no price frame whatsoever — the setter conversation went through his girlfriend and no number was pre-set. $9,000 landed cold on someone who had not been anchored at all.

anchors.raw: Actually, was my girlfriend that got in touch with you guys, because... So we had a little while looking for what to do, like training-wise.
anchors.note: The household had already been actively searching for a training solution and the partner initiated contact, so the buying intent is joint rather than solo. The rep confirmed she was '100% on this' — the constraint is cash, not consent.

anchors.raw: I already used kettlebells, so I was just finding a way that I could like, rather than plan for a gym... I used to even travel with a kettlebell. I used to pay a lot on the airline fee, but it was still worth it.
anchors.note: Already owns the equipment, already swings 25 kg, and has a demonstrated history of paying real money for kettlebell access. Modality resistance is zero; only the ticket size is in question.

unmet_demand.want: Training that is safe and appropriate during active radiotherapy and twelve months of chemotherapy, coordinated with his oncology team
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme is a general one-to-one kettlebell coaching offer with no clinical pathway, no oncology-aware programming and no mechanism for obtaining or acting on medical clearance. Nothing on the call established whether Trevor can or should program for someone eight weeks post-craniotomy with a seizure history.

unmet_demand.want: A short, defined preparation block — roughly two months to build capacity before chemotherapy starts
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Only 6- and 12-month terms exist. The prospect stated the two-month window explicitly and the rep did not reconcile it with the terms he then quoted; the 12-month option in particular spans the whole chemotherapy year the prospect cannot predict.

unmet_demand.want: Written payment options he and his partner could sit down and evaluate
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep stated 'we don't have, like, a set payment plans' and made a split conditional on the prospect naming a number first, so nothing was sent and nothing was structured. The company does appear to do instalments case by case, so this is a packaging and articulation failure rather than a missing capability.

unmet_demand.want: Assurance that the training will actually help him withstand treatment — 'if I'm feeling fit, if I'm feeling stronger, I'm more likely to go to the treatment well'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep affirmed this framing enthusiastically rather than qualifying it, but no evidence, protocol or clinical basis exists in the offer to support a claim about treatment tolerance. Whether the programme serves this is genuinely unknown and it is being sold as though it does.
